feat(onchain,sdk,fault-proofs): exact fraud_prover_reward routing, exclusively via RemoveFraudulentBlockHeader (#603)

Riders 4+5 of #579's scope amendment, per the owner's 2026-08-11 ruling 7
with four orchestrator adjudications recorded on #603. D3: the
settlement.ts 60% heuristic and its prover payout are deleted (params
retired so the rule cannot revive); on-chain, the reward routes EXACTLY
— enterprise address from the fraud-proof datum's prover credential
(bound to the computation thread's StepDatum.fraud_prover under the
prover's own Init signature), ADA-only, exact env.fraud_prover_reward,
no reference script — with the prover's signature required exactly on
the reward-bearing case (gated per the post-review ruling; a zero-reward
slash demands no prover cooperation). The residual bond goes to the
transaction fee per F04 §2.3. D4: the reward is payable only via the
bond-consuming slashing arms of RemoveFraudulentBlockHeader —
m_fraud_prover_reward_output_index lives INSIDE SlashActiveOperator/
SlashRetiredOperator so OperatorAlreadySlashed structurally cannot name
a reward output, and additionally refuses reward-shaped outputs.
None-only-at-zero: the exact routing of zero is the absence of an
output (0-lovelace outputs are L1-invalid); payment is mandatory and
exact at every nonzero profile.

F04 §2.3's final bullet is amended (Amendment 3, provenance on #603):
the literal bond-consuming-AND-target-removing pairing is unimplementable
for non-tail blocks — the slash necessarily lands on a successor-pruning
transaction. §2.4's at-most-one-reward boundary is unchanged.

Mutation-verified: exactness (over/under/wrong-credential), structural
exclusivity, the signature gate (both directions — the un-gated shape
reds the zero-profile row), third-party-signature refusal. Off-chain
twins moved in the same change (SDK schema/builder + reward-branch
signer; the CLI's pre-existing submitter==prover preflight retained).
plutus.json byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); the
redeemer wire change and hash movements ride #579: state_queue.mint
9a823d55→1bb1b776, operator-directory mints decoder-only
b37370a3→508f33a1 / 11791af7→b49663ac (fork-baseline, recorded in the
new D3/D4 evidence artifact); +15 frozen-blueprint emulator reds
(named, single mechanism, self-clearing at #579).

feat(onchain,sdk,node,dacn): governor floor ceil(2n/3) with n ≥ 1 — single-key attestation AND governance accepted (#602)

Rider 3 of #579's scope amendment, per the owner's 2026-08-11 ruling 4
plus the 2026-08-13 in-session Option-B ruling (recorded on #602): the
1-of-1 prohibition is lifted at both layers and for BOTH the committee
and the owner set. da-params-governor's floor is now (2·set_len + 2)/3
with no clamp; min_governed_threshold and min_owner_count are deleted
(the empty-set refusal lives structurally in the sorted-unique walkers
and is pinned by test, not by a vacuous guard). A one-owner set signing
alone at update_threshold 1 can rotate the committee and the governed
threshold — pinned POSITIVELY by a real spend-handler test named as an
acceptance. What still refuses, pinned: empty sets, thresholds above
set size, below-floor, zero thresholds (floor ≥ 1 at every n, swept
1..256).

Bootstrap warns instead of rejecting at both layers (rate-limited
10-minute notice on the repeating attest loop; per-bootstrap warnings on
the one-shot init paths, documented as such). F04 §4 amended in
lockstep with both rulings blockquoted verbatim with provenance; the
Q63 gate computes the whole floor itself (no independently-maintained
constant) and gains a required single-owner-governance-consequence
group; the evidence artifact carries the governor hash movement for
#579 (f00f70a2… → eeefbbf4…, 3 entries, 398/702 both sides, zero other
movement, fork-baseline per ruling A; the committee-only intermediate
b54295fb… is superseded). SDK twin unclamped with a symmetric
committee_below_minimum diagnostic. Mutation-verified: restoring either
retired floor reddens exactly the named pins.

plutus.json byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); the
governor hash lands at #579's single regeneration.

feat(onchain,sdk,spec): committed-field-shape fault family — the §12.8 (field_index, preimage) verdicts for the §12.7 residue (#601)

Closes the §12.7 residue per the owner's 2026-08-13 ruling (embedded in
#601): a second decoder-free step family on the da-hash-preimage pattern
whose verdict is a function of (field_index, preimage), convicting the
two operator-committed stall shapes §12.7's bytes-only verdict correctly
refuses to admit — §7.4 wrong-stride at the fixed-stride fields
(0, 1, 3, 4, 7) and §5.4's byte bound (> 32,768). Codes: 0 admissible /
1 not_an_envelope / 2 field_byte_bound / 3 wrong_stride; only 2 and 3
convict, so a §12.7-convictable byte string is rendered here and refused
at step 02 — the partition between the sibling families is in the code.
§12.7's verdict is imported, not restated; the §8.8 door, the carriage
ladder, and the canonical-decodability family are untouched (the only
§12.7 change is +3 residue pins showing both shapes verdict-0,
door-aborting, and convictable under §12.8).

The door agreement is directional, not biconditional: at a fixed-stride
slot whole_view settles §5.1 by arithmetic and never walks items, so
garbage the door opens can render not_an_envelope here — fail-safe
(code 1 never convicts) and pinned as unclaimed in both languages.

DEVIATION (orchestrator Ruling 1, option A): the §7.4 shape convicts
end-to-end at all three §8 tiers; the §5.4 shape convicts at validator
semantics with complete machinery, but no §8 tier can deliver a preimage
above 32,768 bytes (certified_chunks' bound, the §8.6 mint bound, L1
maxTxSize for tiers 1-2), so §5.4 convictions cannot complete against
real L1 until the owner authorizes a carriage mechanism. The residual
hatch is exactly "committed field preimage > 32,768 bytes" — strictly
narrower than before this ticket. Named, not mitigated, in §12.8's own
residue paragraph and the exec ledger.

Both languages with producer-emitted cross-language vectors, exec ledger
(+ CI verifier; §12.7's previously-unwired golden channel wired beside
it), 6/6 key mutations killed including the step-01→step-02 next-step-
hash guard pinned from the start. plutus.json byte-identical
(c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); identity movement recorded for #579:
394 → 398 validators purely additive, 694 → 702 definitions, parity
handoff set 16 → 17.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore(node,l1-services,docs): Kupo ≥2.10.0 — single-request resolve_hashes carriage read, workaround retired (#599)

Owner ruling (2026-08-13, recorded on #599): update the dependency
instead of carrying a local compatibility workaround. l1-services pins
cardanosolutions/kupo v2.9.0 → v2.11.0 (aligning with the devnet phase4
stack's digest-pinned v2.11.0 rather than introducing a third version);
the carriage reader returns to the natural single-request
/matches/{ref}?resolve_hashes contract with inline datums, and
fetchKupoDatumV1 with all two-request plumbing is deleted.

Fail-closed hardened for the new failure mode: a Kupo older than
v2.10.0 ignores the flag and serves matches without a datum field —
the reader now condemns that deployment on the FIRST request with an
error naming the version floor and the compose pin, never a silently
empty carriage. Harness re-modeled on the tagged v2.11.0 OpenAPI
(datum/script present iff the flag is sent; wire-shape pin refuses a
harness generous to flagless requests); corruption negatives re-pinned
through the §4 hash door. Operator docs aligned (deployment-constraints
block + docs-site l1-backend page: floor v2.10.0+, --match "*",
--prune-utxo prohibition retained).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(validation,sdk): open the tiers-2/3 carriage seam — plan-input witnesses with resolution at evidence commitment (#600)

Completes the closure #597 narrowed. The trace producer no longer decides
carriage tiers at all: the four carriage-bearing auxiliary arms carry a
plan input (fieldIndex, fieldPreimage), and the carriage materialises at
evidence commitment, where buildValidationOneStepArgumentV1 takes a
resolver running §8.4's partition planner and the SDK content resolvers —
mandatory above the 14,336 B tier-1 cap, Inline by default below it.
ValidationMachineCarriageTierUnsupportedErrorV1 is retired completely.

This also closes an unrecorded consequence of #597's narrowing: the
producer sits on the operator's block-production path (mpf.ts), so the
named refusal could fail an entire block build for a legal ~14.3 KB
output. Pinned by a regression test that builds a block-path trace over
a 16,388-byte field-2 preimage with no resolver and no L1 context.

The seam is structural, not conventional: resolver output is checked
against the partition (tier mismatch refuses) and tier-1 bytes must be
identical to the plan input's preimage (substitution refuses); both
named errors are pinned by mutation-verified negatives. §8.7 indices
come only from content resolution against the door-running transaction's
complete reference-input set; assertMidgardFieldCarriageResolvesAtDoorV1
guards layout divergence (unit-pinned; production wiring rides #579's
tiers-2/3 emulator leg). C21's ±8 O(1) closure is restored across the
admissible range — measured auxiliary 10 B at a 14,778 B preimage and
14 B at 16,388 B, vs 14,795 B for the tier-1 maximum — with the chunked
fallback re-pinned by an exercising trace.

Wire moved nothing: the ValidationAuxiliaryWitnessV1 schema, Plutus
Constr encoding, and ABI corpus hash are byte-identical; plutus.json
unchanged (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5). Two producer-emitted
cross-language vectors (RawUtxo, Certified) land against the source
Aiken door with decoy-resistant content-resolved indices; the tiers-2/3
emulator leg is #579's by construction (frozen-blueprint red set stays
at 5, per ruling).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(node): source forced-order §8 carriage from a node-local Ogmios chain-sync read (#599)

Ends the #594 refusal: the node's forced-order ingestion can now supply
the carriage its authenticator demands. Per the owner's 2026-08-13 ruling
the source is node-local and Ogmios+Kupo only — no watcher dependency:
Kupo's match gives the order's created_at {slot_no, header_hash}; an
Ogmios chain-sync session (findIntersection at an ancestor checkpoint,
nextBlock to the matching header) yields the creating transaction's mint
redeemer; reference-input carriage resolves through Kupo's v2.9.0-shaped
Match (datum_hash/datum_type) plus GET /datums/{hash} — deliberately not
the ≥2.10.0 ?resolve_hashes contract, so the reader speaks what the
pinned deployment serves. Every observed byte still terminates in
reconstructTxOrderMaterialV1's three-tier §4 hash door; corruption,
outage, and rollback all fail closed (delay, never mis-ingest). The read
is skipped for canonically-empty orders (commitment-derived, so a
material-bearing order can never take the skip path).

Tests: a local Ogmios (real RFC6455 WebSocket) + Kupo (real HTTP) harness
over real signed emulator transactions; all three §8 tiers ingest
end-to-end from the observation, including a DB-backed reconciler pass;
corruption negatives pin the fail-closed door. The refusal path and the
Kupmios-surface docstring section are removed, not reworded. Operator
constraints documented: --match "*", no --prune-utxo (§8.7 reclaim vs
§8.11 normative history), v2.x /datums contract.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(sdk,validation,fault-proofs,node): the TypeScript wire twin of #592's machine move — carriage-borne auxiliary witnesses and the preimage proof-item datum (#597)

Ends the frozen-blueprint silent divergence for #592's moved machine wire
types on the TypeScript side. The four auxiliary witness constructors
(indices 1, 2, 29, 30) and ValidationProofItemDatumV1 now carry
FieldCarriageV1 / field_preimage exactly as the Aiken source declares
(validation-machine-v1.ak:119,127,303,313,421), plus the moved
CanonicalDecodeItemObservationV1 shape; the encoder gains fieldCarriageData
(Inline 0 / RawUtxo 1 / Certified 2); verifyMachineFieldItemV1 retires
with its seven mutation rows; thirteen emission sites (the issue's
"twelve" is a miscount against its own enumeration) route through one
fieldCarriage closure.

Tier policy per orchestrator Ruling 1 (option C): the trace producer
derives the tier from §8.4's selectMidgardFieldCarriageTierV1, emits
Inline only when admitted (≤ 14,336 B), and refuses above the cap with
the named ValidationMachineCarriageTierUnsupportedErrorV1 — never a
carriage §8.4 does not admit, never fabricated reference-input indices.
The tiers-2/3 producer path is #600 (blocked_by #597, blocks #579).
Per Ruling 2 the C21 proof-fit probes re-pin the real tier-1 property —
auxiliary ≤ preimage + CBOR segment framing, no per-item proof material —
with the above-cap probes pinned to the named refusal; #600 restores the
O(1) form.

Recorded for #579: the parity suite cannot see this wire change even
after regeneration (ValidationAuxiliaryWitnessV1 hits a recursive ABI
definition; ValidationProofItemDatumV1 never reaches a declared ABI
surface) — coverage is the cross-language producer vector instead.
plutus.json byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); the two
touched .ak files are generator-owned and producer-emitted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain,sdk,spec): canonical-decodability fault family — the §12.7 decoder-free step family on the da-hash-preimage pattern (#596)

Closes the operator escape hatch #593's owner Ruling 2 named: under §4 the
operator commits blake2b_256(arbitrary bytes) per field, and the §8.8 door
correctly aborts on committed bytes that are not a §5.1 envelope — so no
CanonicalDecode step was producible by anyone and the dispute stalled. The
new family convicts "the committed preimage of field i is not a §5.1
envelope" directly: the prover supplies the committed bytes, hash-checked
against the commitment via the new non-aborting
authenticated_committed_preimage reader (never reachable through either
door entry point — the door's abort semantics are byte-identical), and a
two-step validator family renders the grammar verdict and convicts.

- docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §12.7: the fault kind, its adjudication, the
  disjointness boundary against §12.3's fault_item_predicate
  (reject_field_preimage_size / reject_invalid_field_type stay
  CanonicalDecode's), and the named residue recorded for the owner.
- Aiken: canonical-decodability rule + steps 01/02 (80 selectors, 15
  guard refusals — 13 isolated, 2 backstops, mutation-verified), producer
  fixtures, exec ledger with verifier wired into CI.
- TypeScript: canonical-decodability-v1 builder/verifier twins with
  producer-emitted cross-language vectors (both artifacts checked).
- Identity movement recorded for #579 rider 6: 390 → 394 validators,
  purely additive; plutus.json byte-identical
  (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); parity handoff set 14 → 16.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain,sdk,node,watcher): forced-order material carriage on the field-access door (#594)

Executes the 2026-08-11 owner ruling (supersedes #589/#583): forced
orders carry their material as prover-chosen per-field FieldCarriageV1
in the tx-order mint redeemer, authenticated at mint against the
compact's nine §4 commitments.

On-chain: verify_order_material walks §2.5's nine slots and opens the
§8.8 door at each non-empty commitment - the all-empty clause and its
"cannot be wired from this lane" note are gone. The vector is
positional over non-empty slots with exhaustion refused in both
directions, declared-length-vs-authenticated-length bound, the
empty-slot declared_length == 1 rule enforced, and burns carrying no
vector. TxOrderPayloadV1 unchanged (§8.7: carriage is identified by
digests, never OutputReference). The mint wraps the shared user-events
redeemer and gains field_preimage_certificate_policy_id (the same §8.6
deployment role as #592's machine parameter; churn recorded for #579).
The door entry point is the whole-materialising one - mutation-proven
load-bearing: the lazy tier-3 view never hashes the chunk bytes this
mint would otherwise vouch for, and spec §8.11 now says so normatively.
Tests 8 -> 35 in the module: positive + negative per tier, wrong-bytes
per constructor (same-stride so the hash is the sole falsifier,
mutation-verified), plus the empty-slot and burn refuters.

Spec: new §8.11 (durable availability = L1 history + digest addressing;
prover-chosen carriage at the order mint; creator payment-key custody,
unconditional reclaim, script credentials refused; the empty-slot and
burn rules; §8.7 citation corrected from the ruling text's §8.5).

Off-chain: the watcher decodes the wrapped redeemer for the tx-order
policy (bare enum for the other three) with an old-shape negative; the
node ingestion walk opens the TS door per non-empty slot re-deriving
the mint's exhaustion rule, Inline carriage live end-to-end
(material-chain 12/12 incl. a Certified row); order-creation planning
chooses inline vs predeploy-and-reference per field, publications
target the creator's wallet, tier-3-without-policy-id throws. AC5's
RawUtxo/Certified ingestion remainder is deviation-recorded and
re-homed to #599 (blocked_by this ticket; the Kupmios provider surface
- 14 methods, none returning a tx body - cannot supply the creation
tx's redeemer; premise independently verified twice). Receipt-family
retirement (AC3) proven already satisfied by #587 with grep evidence.

Measurement: new tx-order-mint exec ledger (4 rows, worst admissible
shape, neutralisation selectors mutation-verified, CI-wired) pins
§8.11's cost claim per the gate-that-cannot-fail doctrine; the four
existing ledgers pass without --update (the mint is not on any
measured path). Applied-hash delta for #579: head 887f814f -> work
56af1ae7, 2 changed entries = tx_order_v1.mint (params
[hub_oracle] -> [hub_oracle, field_preimage_certificate_policy_id]),
recorded on #579 superseding #587's one-parameter note. Also recorded:
the F05 27-path/17-unleased enumeration, two stale evidence citations,
and the fork-binary provenance discrepancy (CI pin 6d14ab2 vs rider 1's
2a78108) for owner reconciliation at the compiler switch.

Verification: fork full check 2,308 / 0 errors (+27 attributed);
adversarial review round 1 (5 majors + 12 minors, all fixed or
evidence-rebutted - deposit-flow-emulator independently re-run 14/14
green with the lane applied, the 13/1 observation matching a
foreign-stamped shared-Postgres signature) + CLEAN confirmation round
with an independent whole_view mutation check; watcher 62/62 with tsc
clean; parity 8/22 (30) and the emulator-shared handoff comment at
FOURTEEN, both run-verified; both formatters idempotent on touched .ak;
plutus.json byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); no
parent-only surface touched. Orchestrator ruling this iteration: #599's
edge re-pointed to blocked_by #594 per the #587/#589 precedent (the
remainder is a node feature, not blueprint-identity work), so this
ticket closes under its recorded Deviation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain,validation): rebind the validation machine onto the authenticated field door; repair E1 (#592)

The last compiled-code unit before #579's single blueprint regeneration:
every counted per-item opening in the validation machine moves onto the
authenticated flat field door, executing #593's owner rulings (tiers
1-3 for machine-step evidence; committed-garbage aborts stay with
#596's fault family; E1 repaired in this lane).

The rebind. All fifteen counted opening sites across eight machine
phases (CanonicalDecode, InputSets, Signatures, PhaseANativeScripts,
PhaseAScriptPreconditions, ScriptSources stages 0/1/4/mint/7, Cek) -
reached through four ValidationAuxiliaryWitnessV1 constructors, one
more than the ticket's measured table - are gone:
bounded_collection_v1.verify_item occurrences in validation-machine-v1
drop 41 -> 2 (a bare constant). New lib
validation-machine-field-door-v1.ak (MachineFieldDoorV1 carrying
reference_inputs + certificate_policy_id, open_machine_field_item{,_at},
machine_field_count, derived readers - every byte returned only via
field_read_range over an authenticated view) plus
native_tx_field_access_v1.authenticated_whole_field_view, the
materializing tier-3 view the count-consuming phases need (one
blake2b_256 over the whole preimage against the §4 commitment; the
shared prologue is factored so the §2.5 pairing has one spelling).
ValidationProofItemDatumV1 carries the whole §5.1 field_preimage
(wrapped as Inline inside the validator - no prover-named tier);
CanonicalDecodeItemObservationV1 reshaped and its predicate renamed
_is_consistent to say what it proves. Twelve validation-trace
validators gain field_preimage_certificate_policy_id (last position);
canonical_decode_item_semantic_v1 moves for a redeemer reshape. A
latent defect fixed en route: transaction_field_item_encoded_length was
stale since #567 and one negative was accepting the wrong successor it
claimed to reject.

The E1 repair (in scope per the binding ruling). chunk_bytes_k and
MIDGARD_CHUNK_BYTES_K_V1 move 15,900 -> 15,148, closing §8.3 erratum
E1's unpublishable window as a property of the repair (drift guard: a
literal K - MAX_PUBLISHABLE == 0). Everything K touches re-derived from
producers: the #569 straddle vector ([15,148, 855], straddling item
378), the #568 goldens, the §8.10 corner ([15,148, 15,148, 2,467]),
~30 spec rows, the §12.5 tier-2 fixtures, the carriage exec ledger
(re-taken; binding axis flips CPU -> memory at 83.54%), and the
carriage-fit emulator (16/16). The 16,225 B measured-maximum field-2
preimage now splits [15,148, 1,077] - both chunks publishable - and the
max-inline-datum row greens via a real tier-3 Certified manifest
asserting exactly that admissibility, not a tier-1 evidence shape no
prover could construct. #598 closed as absorbed (it had been filed on
the authority of a retracted comment).

Verification. Fork-runner full check 2,281 checks / 0 errors / 7
warnings - the 22-row #592 family greens and the Aiken side of the
repo is fully green for the first time in the program; the +1 test is
a new negative making item_count == active_total_count a real
falsifier. Adversarial soundness review CLEAN: all 15 sites verified
guard-for-guard, negatives mutation-tested, no reader returns
unauthenticated bytes (the #575 forgery class), no tier smuggling
through the datum wrap. Exec ledgers pass without --update with
accuracy-audited cause notes (two distinct per-opening amounts: body
+2,224/+682,801, witness +2,124/+666,801; the q21 two-body-opening
total 4,248 = 2x the witness figure is published as measured, no false
derivation; carriage figures labeled cumulative vs round-4-only).
Isolated stock-build delta reproduced twice: 390 entries both trees, 73
changed entries across 36 distinct validators, head 0ad09746 / work
887f814f - what #579's applied-hash cascade inherits, with the
cert-parameter arity churn recorded on #579 (rider 2), never edited.
plutus.json byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); no
parent-only surface touched; both formatters idempotent on all touched
.ak; producer --check chains clean; scanner-doc (#571) reconciliation
proven neutral. Follow-up #597 (the TS wire twin of the four moved
constructors + datum, indivisible across four packages, currently a
silent divergence because parity reads the frozen blueprint) is filed,
blocked_by this ticket, blocking #579.

fix(onchain): unpin the retired 36-byte out-ref key from the InputSets machine phase (#592)

Landed while #592's rebind was measured indivisible and re-homed to
#593 for rulings: the InputSets phase pinned the retired 36-byte
out-ref key at two sites (encode_input_sets_scan_witness's domain
assertion and input_sets_control_is_bound) while verify_input_sets_item
reads previous_key off the §5.3 item it decodes - 38 bytes since #586 -
so the phase crashed inside its own witness encoder on any step that
had read one input. Both sites now name
native_tx_field_access_v1.spend_input_item_bytes; the two affected
baseline rows move from "program failed" aborts to a clean False on the
counted conjunct, so all 22 owned rows now fail for exactly the one
#592 cause. Plus the countedMachineFieldTraceV1 docstring gains the
measured both-halves size and the #593 pointer.

Verification: fork-runner full check 1686 / 22 failed, byte-identical
by name to #585's baseline; isolated stock builds (v1.1.22+39d6b04,
env -u MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN) show exactly 4 changed entries / 2 named
validators (input_sets_empty_semantic_v1, input_sets_item_semantic_v1)
- recorded on #592 for #579's applied-hash cascade; in-tree plutus.json
byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); exec ledgers pass
without --update (no measured row exercises InputSets); stock-fmt CI
sim idempotent on the edited .ak; tsc/prettier clean;
validation-machine source-text suites 11/11.

#592 remains open: the rebind is one indivisible unit (15 sites, 8
phases, one TransactionFieldChunkWitness constructor) blocked on #593's
two rulings (which §8 tiers a machine step may name - tier-1's 14,336 B
bound vs the 16,225 B measured maximum field-2 preimage inside erratum
E1's window - and how an ungrammatical committed preimage is rejected
rather than aborted under the §4 door).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(core,sdk,validation,lucid,node,watcher): the nine-field consumer swap onto flat commitments (#585)

The flat-reversion centerpiece: the counted scheme dies TypeScript-side.
The first attempt (#578's measurement) was reverse-applied as
worse-than-either-end; this landing follows the three blockers it
surfaced - #586 (ledger out-ref unification), #587 (receipt chain
retirement), #588 (producer machinery) - so the swap ships as one
coherent unit.

midgard-core: all nine field derivations in native-body.ts /
native-witness.ts move to midgardFieldCommitmentV1 over §5.1 preimage
bytes; validateMidgardNativeTxCanonicalV1 is the §5.1 fail-closed
grammar walk at the encoder, canonical decoder and materialisation;
native-field-items.ts deleted (§5.1 collapses its three-way split);
verifyMidgardV1TxFieldPreimage flat; the counted per-item publication
surface (deriveMidgardV1TxFieldChunks/Evidence, verify chunk/item,
reconstruct-from-chunks, both evidence types) deleted; fields 5/6/8
into the §5.1 envelope; sortMidgardMintItemsV1 gives §5.6's two-level
